faq.question: Is Seedream 5.0 Pro uncensored for NSFW images?
faq.answer: Yes. Pro’s generation and editing do not require a content flag; layer separation still has the model-side refusals documented in our SpicyAPI tests. Unfiltered editorial runs on the same text-to-image and editing endpoints as everything else.

faq.question: How is Seedream 5.0 Pro different from 5.0 Lite?
faq.answer: Pro spends more on material detail and frames the image with an aspect ratio plus a 1k, 1.5k or 2k tier. Lite names the frame with an explicit width*height preset instead — eight of them, all at the 2K tier. Pick Pro for the finishing frame, Lite when the placement is specified as a preset.

faq.question: How many reference images can one edit take?
faq.answer: Up to ten. Assign a role to each in the prompt, because unnamed sources get blended. Every reference beyond the first adds to the quote you see before submitting.

faq.question: What does the resolution tier change?
faq.answer: Both the pixel count and the price band. 2k is the default and the tier for delivery. 1.5k carries roughly twice the pixels of 1k and costs less than 2k, so it is the working tier when 2k is more than the job needs; 1k is the quick pass for checking a composition before you commit to the full frame.

faq.question: Can I set the output size or aspect ratio?
faq.answer: Yes, as a ratio and a tier rather than free pixels. aspect_ratio takes fifteen shapes from 1:3 to 3:1, and resolution picks 1k, 1.5k or 2k. Text-to-image defaults to 1:1; editing defaults to auto, which picks the supported ratio closest to your first reference. If you need a named width*height preset, use Seedream 5.0 Lite.

faq.question: Is there a seed for reproducible results?
faq.answer: No. Neither endpoint exposes one, so two identical requests return two different frames. Keep the prompt stored with any asset you intend to reuse.

faq.question: Which Seedream 5.0 Pro output format should I use for further design work?
faq.answer: png when the frame goes on into retouching or compositing and lossless edges matter; jpeg for review loops and direct delivery. It changes the file you receive, not the image that was generated.

faq.question: What should I check in a Seedream 5.0 Pro text-heavy layout?
faq.answer: ByteDance describes stronger text rendering and complex information layouts as Pro capabilities. Use checked copy in your design brief, then inspect the actual lettering and small text before publication; the official positioning is not a guarantee of error-free output.

faq.question: Can Seedream 5.0 Pro split an image into layers?
faq.answer: Yes, through the separate Layer Decomposition endpoint. It takes one finished image and returns a base plate plus up to sixteen transparent PNG layers, each with a position box and a name, so you can put the pieces back exactly where they came from or rearrange them. Unfiltered source images can be split, from Mild up to Strong and at Maximum. Source images at the Very strong level are declined by the model, with no charge. It is billed per output image at $0.042 for 1k and 1.5k and $0.084 for 2k and auto, with the base plate counted as one image.

howTo.title: Decide whether you are generating or assembling
howTo.body: No references means text-to-image; one to ten references means the editing endpoint, where the frame follows the first reference unless you set aspect_ratio. Both accept the same 5,000-character prompt, so the choice is about starting material, not about rewriting the brief.

howTo.title: Write the treatment, then set the frame
howTo.body: Subject, wardrobe, light source and direction, lens, grade. Then choose the aspect ratio and the 1k, 1.5k or 2k tier. The portrait on this page came from: "High-resolution beauty editorial photograph, close portrait of an adult woman with wet hair slicked back, water beading on her collarbone and bare shoulders, a heavy ivory silk robe slipping off one shoulder, arms folded across her chest, dramatic single softbox from camera left, glossy skin texture, deep black background, luxury fragrance campaign look."

howTo.title: Poll the task and keep the brief with the asset
howTo.body: Keep the Pro prompt, resolution and accepted result together after the task finishes; for a separated design also retain each layer’s name and bounding box. With no seed field there is no way to redraw an exact frame, so store the prompt alongside the result you keep.

features.title: Wet skin, silk and candle shadow that hold up close
features.body: This is the tier where texture stops being implied and starts being rendered: water beading on a collarbone, the weight of heavy silk, the falloff of a single softbox against a black ground. It is the reason to spend a call here rather than on a faster sibling once a direction is already settled.

features.title: Merge a face, a garment and a room in one edit
features.body: The editing endpoint accepts one to ten reference images. Assign each a role in the prompt — subject from the first, garment from the third, room from the fifth — and it composes them into a single frame. Each extra reference adds to the quote, and the estimate you see before submitting is what settles.

features.title: Fifteen ratios, and edits that keep the source's shape
features.body: aspect_ratio runs from 1:3 to 3:1 — fifteen shapes, including 4:5 for feeds and 21:9 for a banner — and resolution picks the 1k, 1.5k or 2k tier. On the editing endpoint the default is auto: the output takes the supported ratio closest to the first reference, so a portrait source comes back as a portrait unless you ask for another shape.

useCases.title: Uncensored editorial finals
useCases.body: Candlelit interiors, wet-look beauty portraits, silk in hard light — the frames a campaign actually ships. There is no maturity flag to set and no separate endpoint: the same two endpoints handle a fragrance still and an unfiltered final identically.

useCases.title: Beauty and fragrance campaign stills
useCases.body: Single hard softbox, deep black ground, glossy skin and water detail. The material rendering is close enough that a comp survives a client review instead of being explained away as a placeholder.

useCases.title: Ten-reference scene assembly
useCases.body: Send a subject photograph, two garment references, a props plate and a location shot in one editing call, and name what each contributes. One request replaces a compositing session, and the lighting is matched by the model rather than by hand.

useCases.title: Finishing pass on a settled direction
useCases.body: Explore composition on a faster model, then bring the wording that worked here for the frame you intend to deliver. The prompt does not need restructuring — only the reference set, the aspect ratio and the resolution tier are worth revisiting.

limits.body: There is no seed and no free width*height field: framing comes from aspect_ratio, which is 1:1 unless you set it, and from the 1k, 1.5k or 2k resolution tier. Two identical requests will not return identical frames, so keep the brief and the returned asset together rather than expecting to regenerate a result later.

One to ten references, and roles have to be assigned in the prompt — unnamed sources get blended into a compromise. aspect_ratio defaults to auto, the supported ratio closest to the first reference, so put the image whose shape you want to keep first or name a ratio yourself. Each extra reference beyond the first adds to the quote. Long chains of edits drift, so re-edit from the original frame rather than from the previous output.

Before delivering a Pro composition or reusing its separated layers, clear the source rights and review the final publication. Only consenting adults may be depicted; non-consensual material and deceptive impersonation are prohibited, and these requirements do not imply that every request is screened.

familyContent.closing: Seedream 5.0 Pro is ByteDance's high-detail Seedream image model, published as two endpoints: text-to-image, and image-to-image reading one to ten reference images. Both take a prompt of up to 5,000 characters, one of fifteen aspect ratios, a 1k, 1.5k or 2k resolution tier and a jpeg or png output format; the editing endpoint defaults to auto framing, which follows the first reference. Neither exposes a seed, so results are not reproducible call to call. Billing is per output image by resolution tier, with each additional reference priced into an edit. It is the tier for finishing frames — wet skin, silk, candle shadow, ten-source scene assembly — and it runs uncensored, with no maturity flag and no prompt scanner.

data.description:
## What this endpoint does

Seedream 5.0 Pro Text to Image turns a written treatment into a single image. What separates it from faster models is material: wet skin, heavy fabric, candle falloff and specular detail that hold up when someone looks closely.

## Inputs that matter

`prompt` holds up to 5,000 characters — enough for subject, wardrobe, light source and direction, lens and grade in one pass. `aspect_ratio` sets the shape from fifteen options between `1:3` and `3:1` and defaults to `1:1`, so a request that leaves it out comes back square. `resolution` picks the `1k`, `1.5k` or `2k` tier, and `output_format` picks jpeg or png.

There is no seed field here, so two identical requests still return two different frames.

## Content

Uncensored editorial runs with no flag and no separate endpoint; your wording is passed on to the model as written.

## What you get back

One image per request as a platform asset URL, billed per output image against the estimate shown before submission.

paramNotes.aspect_ratio: 1:1 (the default) or one of fourteen other shapes from 1:3 to 3:1, including 4:5, 21:9 and 9:21. There is no automatic mode on this endpoint — leave it out and the frame comes back square, so name the ratio you are delivering at.
paramNotes.enable_thinking: On by default: the model runs a thinking pass that refines your prompt before generating. Switching it off skips that pass, so text-to-image finishes noticeably faster. No effect on price.
paramNotes.output_format: For Pro layouts with lettering and fine edges, PNG avoids another lossy save; JPEG suits delivery previews, with the same price at a given resolution.
paramNotes.prompt: Up to 5,000 characters. Spend it on light source and direction, material and lens rather than adjectives — this tier renders what you specify and invents what you leave out.
paramNotes.resolution: 1k, 1.5k or 2k; 2k by default. The tier sets both the pixel count and the price band, so it is not just a sharpness knob: 1.5k carries roughly twice the pixels of 1k and costs less than 2k.

prompt.description: Describe the image to generate: subject, composition, style, and lighting.

output_format.description: File format of the returned image.

enable_thinking.description: Run a thinking pass that refines the prompt before generating. Off is faster.

data.readme:
## Introduction

**Seedream 5.0 Pro Text-to-Image** creates a new image from a written design brief. Use it when you need to establish a composition, arrange supplied text or explore a photographic look without starting from an existing picture.

Developed by ByteDance and introduced in its [July 8, 2026 launch article](https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/beyond-generation-it-understands-design-introducing-seedream-5-0-pro), the model supports design-oriented image creation. This mode focuses on deciding what should appear and how it should be arranged.

### Choose a Seedream 5.0 Pro mode by starting material

| Starting material | Mode |
| --- | --- |
| A written art direction or design brief | [Seedream 5.0 Pro Text to Image](/models/seedream-5-0-pro/text-to-image) |
| An approved source image to revise | [Seedream 5.0 Pro Image Editing](/models/seedream-5-0-pro/edit) |
| A finished image whose parts you need separately | [Seedream 5.0 Pro Layer Decomposition](/models/seedream-5-0-pro/layer-decomposition) |

## Key features & Highlights

### Information-rich image design

Seedream 5.0 Pro combines text, diagrams and illustrations in structured compositions. Its layout capabilities address infographics, posters and other designs where the organization of information matters as much as the image itself.

### Localized editing and spatial understanding

The model can interpret where a change belongs and which object it concerns. This supports regional replacements, color and material changes, and sketch-guided edits without requiring a new visual brief for the whole composition.

### Photographic materials and lighting

Image creation emphasizes surface texture, reflections, lighting and portrait detail. These capabilities serve both photographic treatments and rendered scenes, with attention to how materials interact with the surrounding light.

### Multilingual visual content

The model supports multilingual prompts and text rendering, including languages with different scripts and reading directions. This enables localized graphics with language-specific copy and typography.

### Multi-image composition

Separate images can supply subjects, materials, style or layout for a combined result. Layer separation is available as its own endpoint, [Seedream 5.0 Pro Layer Decomposition](/models/seedream-5-0-pro/layer-decomposition); ordinary image generation and editing do not export layers.

## Use cases

### Draft an event poster from final copy

Start with the headline, event details and a simple visual theme. Review the hierarchy and legibility before adding decorative elements or producing a finished campaign asset.

### Visualize a product concept before photography

Describe a proposed object, its materials and the scene around it. Use the result to discuss a direction, not to document an existing product accurately. Switch to editing when an approved product photograph should anchor the work.

### Turn supplied information into a visual explainer

Provide a short, checked list of facts and specify a layout that separates them. Review whether every label and relationship is represented correctly; an attractive diagram still needs factual review.

## Prompt guide & Pro tips

### How to write a layout brief for Seedream 5.0 Pro

Describe the image as a design brief: purpose, composition, exact text, visual treatment and lighting. For text-heavy graphics, give the content a hierarchy rather than presenting an unstructured list of words.

1. Choose the intended format through `aspect_ratio`.
2. Describe where the main subject and text blocks belong.
3. Supply the exact copy in quotation marks.
4. Specify materials, colors and light in concrete terms.

For a vertical book-exchange poster, choose `2:3`:

```text
Create a vertical poster for a neighborhood book exchange.
Use a warm cream background with a dark-green and coral palette.

Place the headline "PASS A BOOK ON" in large dark-green lettering across the upper third.
In the center, show two hands passing a worn paperback, illustrated with cut-paper textures.
Below the illustration, place "Bring one. Find one. Share a story." in smaller type.
At the bottom, add "Saturday · 10 AM–2 PM" as a compact information line.

Keep a clear gap between the headline, illustration and supporting copy.
Use only the supplied text, with no extra badges or invented logos.
```

### How to control text and information hierarchy

Separate the headline, supporting copy and practical information. Specify their relative size and position instead of asking for “beautiful typography.” For a chart or infographic, supply the actual labels and values; do not ask the model to invent factual data to fill the layout.

For localized graphics, provide approved text in the target language and describe the reading order. Proofread the generated lettering before publishing.

### How to describe materials and photographic light

Name the surface and its interaction with light: brushed metal with a soft reflection, frosted glass with light passing through it, or textured paper under side lighting. These details communicate the intended appearance more clearly than stacking terms such as “premium” and “ultra-realistic.”

### Revise the brief before increasing resolution

If the composition feels crowded, simplify the content or assign clearer regions. If the image has the wrong look, revise material and lighting directions. A higher `resolution` changes the output tier; it does not resolve a contradictory design brief.

### Content boundaries

**Seedream 5.0 Pro · Text-to-Image — Uncensored.** SpicyAPI adds no platform-side content filter. Pro’s generation and editing do not require a content flag; layer separation still has the model-side refusals documented in our SpicyAPI tests. Before delivering a Pro composition or reusing its separated layers, clear the source rights and review the final publication. Only consenting adults may be depicted; non-consensual material and deceptive impersonation are prohibited, and these requirements do not imply that every request is screened. [Pro · content policy](/legal/content-policy)

examples.note: `resolution` is `2k` because the brief asks for two materials that fail differently, wet skin and wet marble, inside one hard shaft of light; at the lower tier both drift toward the same polished grey. Steam is used as a compositional cut rather than as decoration - the lower third is given up to vapour so the frame spends its detail budget on the two surfaces that are actually lit. `output_format` is `png` to keep that gradient clean.

input.prompt: Cinematic film still, Roman marble bathhouse. Two-shot on the stepped ledges: a woman in her early thirties sits on the upper step in an opaque terracotta linen bathing top and short linen shorts, lifting a brass basin in both hands and pouring it over her own shoulder so the water sheets down her back; the man on the step below, bare-chested in knee-length linen shorts, looks up at her with his forearms resting on his knees, their faces a hand's breadth apart. Thick steam drifts across the lower frame. One hard clerestory shaft cuts the vapour and catches wet skin and wet Carrara marble alike. 65mm, shallow depth of field, warm amber against stone grey, heavy grain, restrained and tasteful.

examples.note: One unbroken line from shoulder to waist with satin sliding across it: a single continuous surface with almost no edges to hide behind, which is the fabric case this tier is worth spending on. Two light sources are named and they disagree on purpose, cold from the window and warm from inside the room, meeting somewhere along the back. `aspect_ratio` is `3:4` out of the fifteen on offer, and `resolution` is `2k` so the weave holds.

input.prompt: Cinematic film still, a woman sits at a tall window wrapped in champagne satin, seen entirely from behind so the frame is one unbroken line of back; the satin has slipped from the shoulder blade to the small of the back and pools there. Cold morning light from the window, warm lamp from inside. 85mm, shallow depth of field, heavy grain, champagne and slate palette, restrained and tasteful.

input.prompt: High-resolution beauty editorial photograph, close portrait of an adult woman with wet hair slicked back, water beading on her collarbone and bare shoulders, a heavy ivory silk robe slipping off one shoulder, arms folded across her chest, dramatic single softbox from camera left, glossy skin texture, deep black background, luxury fragrance campaign look.

examples.note: The second still on this page: the same endpoint aimed at chiaroscuro and candle falloff rather than skin detail.

input.prompt: Candlelit bedroom at night, dozens of pillar candles on the floor and dresser. An adult woman in a sheer black slip sits on the edge of the bed half-turned away, her silhouette and the curve of her back rendered mostly in warm shadow, a single candle flame sharp in the foreground. Deep amber and black, heavy chiaroscuro, film grain, intimate and restrained, medium format look.

Cinematic film still on the upper deck of a night ferry: an adult man and an adult woman sit on separate benches a few feet apart, both pretending to watch the harbour lights while the wind lifts her scarf toward him. Sodium-orange city glow over deep teal water, fine grain, 2.39:1.

Wide shot of a 1950s dance hall: an adult woman in a sea-green tea dress mid-spin on the crowded floor catches the eye of an adult man leaning by the bandstand, and the space between them is strangely empty. Warm tungsten bulbs, soft haze, pastel costumes, painterly film grain.

An empty candlelit restaurant after closing: an adult woman in a backless black velvet gown sits turned away from the camera, one long glove dropped on the tablecloth, while at the far end of the table an adult man pours two glasses of red wine. Low amber light, deep burgundy walls, slow-shutter candle glow.

A hard monochrome art deco stairwell: an adult woman in a floor-length satin gown descends slowly, a single spotlight throwing her long shadow up the curved wall, one gloved hand trailing the chrome banister. Deep blacks, silvery highlights, classic noir framing.

Low-key portrait of an adult man in an open-collared black silk shirt beside a rain-streaked window, a single candle carving his profile out of the dark while his gaze drifts past the lens. Chiaroscuro, deep umber palette, fine grain.

In a snow-silent birch forest, an adult knight in battered silver armour kneels with his helmet in the crook of his arm before a white stag whose antlers are wrapped in faint light. Muted winter palette, volumetric shafts through the trunks, painterly realism.

Menswear campaign: an adult man in an oversized sand-coloured double-breasted suit stands in a desert dust storm, the fabric whipping sideways, dark glasses on, the sun a pale disc behind the haze. Monochrome warm palette, high-fashion finish.
